items.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | 1:1 TECHNOLOGY IS COMING TO ALL FHSD MIDDLE & HIGH SCHOOLS Every middle and high school student gets their own take-home Chromebook this fall. Elementary stays with classroom carts. IF IT SOUNDS TOO GOOD TO BE TRUE… IT IS. DO THEY REALLY THINK WE’RE THAT STUPID? The district says this will “save $300,000 a year.” Reality check: • Damage & loss rates jump when devices go home every day (8–12% annually) • Hardware is only ~25% of the real cost — repairs, IT support, and replacements eat the rest • Other districts have spent tens of millions fixing broken Chromebooks that only last 2–3 years • Parents still get hit with repair/replacement fees They also claim “no more screen time.” Giving every middle & high schooler a personal device makes that hard to believe. More screens. Higher long-term costs. This is not a win for students or taxpayers. CONTACT: board@fhsdschools.org | ZtfCv1cn.com

items.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | CARL DROPS THE MATH HAMMER ON PROP H Schooling the District on “Free Money” VOTE NO on Prop H The ballot will say $150 million. That’s only the face value of the bonds — not the real cost to taxpayers. We’ve seen this before. Prop S in 2020 said $244 million. The final price tag? $294 million. That’s $50 MILLION MORE than voters approved! How did they do it? They intentionally set higher-than-market interest rates so investors would pay a “premium.” The district got extra cash upfront. Taxpayers get stuck with higher interest payments for the next 10–20 years. The district will try to call that extra $50 million “free money.” There is no such thing as free money. It’s basic time value of money. The mathematics hasn’t changed. They can pick whatever number they want — they just need to be transparent about the true total cost. So far, they’re still refusing to do that. Until the district tells taxpayers the real maximum amount they’ll actually spend, Vote No on Prop H. Share this so more people know what’s really at stake. Listen to common sense Carl >>> https://www.youtube.com/live/gXJwYo-H72c?si=gyq68CnaB67WC4Ju&t=280 | rzJuFq.com

items.author: School Watchlist
items.bodyText: BOOKS WITH SEXUAL CONTENT RETAINED Francis Howell parents, a formal challenge was filed. The book in question was: Me, Earl and the Dying Girl by Jesse Andrews This book contains: • Extensive, frequent profanity throughout (including multiple uses of the f-word and other strong language) • Crude and explicit sexual discussions and jokes • Extended, vulgar dialogue about oral sex • Chapters titled “Phone Sex” • Objectifying and crude comments about girls’ bodies • References to masturbation and other sexual topics treated as punchlines • Misogynistic and degrading humor from the teenage male narrators The complaint centered on the language and content. The committee acknowledged the profanity but decided that, taken as a whole, the book supports “academic learning” and is “not pervasively vulgar or objectively offensive.” EM”PATHETIC” REVIEW They “felt” the crude language is similar to what students might hear in daily life. The Review Committee’s decision: Retain without Restrictions – Currently High School Review Committee members included: Jon Schultz (Principal), Diane Thompson (tutor), Zachary Howard (Tennis Coach), Kim Coil, Amy Gryder (Board Member), Susan Schneider, Karin Robinette, Brittany Kreifels IMPORTANT FOR PARENTS: If you do NOT want your child to have access to this type of content at school, you must contact your school's media specialist (librarian) or your child's principal. Written notification is required. Without it, your child will have full access to any book the school deems appropriate, even material such as this. I've said this before, and I'll say it again: we no longer live in an age where adults are protecting children from sexual content. We are living in an age where adults are offering minor children books with age-inappropriate sexual content under the guise of education. #ProtectFHSDKids #ParentsRights #RaisingTheStandard #DontMessWithOurKids

items.bodyText: THIS 1:1 TECH POLICY SHOULDN’T BE HAPPENING TO OUR KIDS Francis Howell middle and high school students are required to take home district Chromebooks starting August 26 for FHN and carry them every single day. Extra weight in already heavy backpacks + more mandatory screen time is a direct hit on kids’ bodies and minds. Physical: Research consistently shows backpacks exceeding 10-15% of a student’s body weight increase neck, shoulder, and back pain plus postural problems. https://www.healthychildren.org/.../Backpack-Safety.aspx Emotional: Higher screen time is linked to increased anxiety and depression symptoms in adolescents. https://www.frontiersin.org/.../fpubh.2023.1101594/full Parents — push back. Email the Board of Education at board@fhsdschools.org and ask them to reconsider mandatory daily Chromebook carry and the added physical + emotional burden this places on students.

items.bodyText: URGENT: School Board Members Celebrating Calls for Violence Against a Parent This is the level of “public education” leadership we are dealing with in Francis Howell. A post from the page “No to Francis Howell Families for FHSD” openly celebrated the idea that an entire group of women “would happily yeet Lauren out of the nearest window.” Yeet = to throw something (or someone) with force. In plain English: they are joking about throwing a parent out a window. That is a call for violence. That is wishing harm on a mother. And what did the newly elected do? • Sara Dillard (current FHSD School Board member) gave it a heart. Sara Dillard - Director, Francis Howell Board of Education https://www.facebook.com/share/19UkKS1T9T/?mibextid=wwXIfr • Ren Boehms Adams (wife of newly elected board member Jason Adams and Theater Director at FH Middle) jumped in and claimed the post as “that’s me!!” Jason Adams for FHSD @Ren Boehms Adams https://www.facebook.com/share/14owBPCEkqH/?mibextid=wwXIfr • Jen Bahr (wife of re-elected St. Charles Director of Elections @kurt Bahr) and recently elected Cottleville Township committee woman, and associated with their Bahr family properties real estate @Jen Bahr https://www.facebook.com/share/1EiDTqGJ21/?mibextid=wwXIfr Citizens for Kurt Bahr Multiple others piled on with likes. To every single person who liked or loved that comment — including Sara Dillard, Ren Boehms Adams and Jen Bahr: Do you support throwing a parent out a window? Are you in favor of a parent’s death or serious harm? If the answer is no, then why didn’t you condemn it? Why did you celebrate it instead? This is not “online banter.” This is elected officials and their spouses normalizing violent rhetoric against a mother who simply advocated for her children and other parents in this district. Francis Howell School District and Board: this must be stopped and dealt with immediately. This is a call to Publicly remove these people from their leadership positions, condemn this behavior and the board members and family members who celebrated it. Silence is approval.

items.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | SHOCK STUDY: STRONGEST GENDER-IDEOLOGY BELIEVERS MORE LIKELY TO SAY POLITICAL VIOLENCE IS JUSTIFIED New HHS-commissioned study (Rutgers, Manhattan Institute, Network Contagion Research Institute) surveyed 1,208 U.S. adults. Key findings: • Strong support for “gender-affirming” clinical positions was tightly linked to left-wing authoritarianism — not just being liberal. • That profile includes aggression toward “oppressors,” support for top-down censorship, and hostility to conventional sex/family norms. • Both gender-ideology endorsement and left-wing authoritarianism predicted greater justification of political violence — including the killings of Charlie Kirk and Brian Thompson, a hypothetical assassination of President Trump, ICE arson, property destruction, and violence against police. • Those links held even after researchers controlled for political identity. The authors say gender ideology may act as an “accelerant”: it names enemies, creates urgency, and makes force feel legitimate to people already inclined toward it. This measured attitudes (who they say violence is justified against), not who has committed violence. Correlation, not proven cause. Sources: https://health.gov/hhs-releases-study-finding-individuals-who-associate-left-wing-authoritarian-beliefs-and-radical https://opa.hhs.gov/gender-ideology-and-left-wing-authoritarianism Full report: https://opa.hhs.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/gender-ideology-report.pdf | u5YZK727J.com

items.bodyText: 21-YEAR WENTZVILLE HOLT TEACHER. FORCED OUT. ZERO NEA UNION DEFENSE. The teacher (Erin) says Wentzville is self-insured and her prior cancer treatments cost the district hundreds of thousands. She alleges Supt. Brian Bishop told the full Board he believed her cancer had returned. She is cancer-free. Remission this November. She says they isolated her with a gag order, muzzled staff, and she had zero representation in the meetings that decided her career. She did not even learn they were accusing her of “kidnapping” an 18-year-old until after she was forced to resign. No police report. No nurse statement. No video (Bishop admitted it). Parents did not complain. She was still recovering from treatment. She says they used that window of duress to push her into a one-of-a-kind separation agreement that waived the tenure rights Missouri law gives every tenured teacher. Her NEA attorney told her to sign. Read her account and the Google Docs: https://www.facebook.com/574279348/posts/10165128816159349/ And FB: https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1EiAFfTZ99/?mibextid=wwXIfr Ask the Board — and the lawyer whose firm still represents WSD — to answer this in public. Board: jonigoodwin@wsdr4.org District: info@wsdr4.org Supt. Brian Bishop: brianbishop@wsdr4.org Pat Brazill (Mickes, DeBeer & Brazill): pat@moconed.com Demand a public explanation of the health comments to the Board, the gag order, why she was kept from the accusation until after she signed, and why a tenured teacher was told to waive her statutory rights.

items.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | ONE LAST DETAIL… A 21-year Holt High teacher didn’t want to leave. Wentzville School District Wentzville’s superintendent reframed her forced exit as an act of kindness. • After the board started questioning contradictions in his first version of events, Supt. Brian Bishop pivoted. • He told them she wanted to resign and he was being “benevolent” by letting her do clerical work so she could keep insurance while battling cancer. • He already had her signature on a separation agreement with a full liability waiver so she could never sue. • She has been clear from the beginning: she did not want to lose her job. • The original “kidnapped a student” claim was a lie. Multiple people had to cooperate for that story to hold. • NEA-endorsed board members voted to accept her “resignation” under that false framing. None have come forward. • 21 years of dues. Zero NEA union defense. The district has quietly authorized payouts and legal covers for administrative failures. A teacher showing basic kindness to a student got shown the door. Full post: https://www.facebook.com/share/p/14vZKzsfCp4/ | XtyBUHVEv.com

items.bodyText: HOLLENBECK ASST. PRINCIPAL ARRESTED FOR CHILD PORNOGRAPHY FHSD just notified families. Hollenbeck Middle School Assistant Principal Daniel “Danny” Ott was arrested after school yesterday. The district says law enforcement intends to charge him with crimes related to possession of child pornography. He has been the assistant principal at Hollenbeck since 2024. Before that, he was an assistant principal at North Point Middle School in the Wentzville School District. FHSD says officers confirmed there is no indication at this time that any Hollenbeck students are involved. He has been placed on leave and is not allowed on any District property until this is resolved. These are allegations. He is innocent until proven guilty. Read the district notice yourself and ask questions if your child had regular contact with him. I applaud the district for being transparent and quick to respond to this matter. Last year similar incidents occurred involving different teachers and we never got the full story.

items.bodyText: HOLLENBECK THREAT UPDATE — NO CREDIBLE THREAT Parents — FYI on Hollenbeck. A social media/text threat targeting the school for Tuesday circulated Friday. St. Charles County Police and FHSD investigated the same day. Police identified a juvenile who admitted sending the original text. They determined the juvenile had no means to carry it out and that no known/credible threat exists. Extra officers will still be at Hollenbeck on Tuesday as a precaution. School is scheduled to be in session Tuesday. Use the official updates and decide what’s best for your family. If you see something new, report it to police — don’t amplify the original messages.

items.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | September 10, 2025, changed America’s history forever. One year ago, our founder, our leader, and our friend, Charlie Kirk, was assassinated while doing what he had devoted his life to: standing before young Americans and challenging them to think, speak, and have the courage to stand for what they believe. There are no words that can adequately describe what this past year has been like. We have had to learn how to carry on without the person at the center of everything we do. We have celebrated milestones Charlie should have been here to celebrate, stood on stages where his voice should have been heard, and watched his children grow without their father there to see it. For those who knew and loved Charlie, September 10 will never simply be an anniversary. It is the day our lives changed forever. Today, our hearts are especially with Erika, Charlie’s children, the Kirk family, and the countless people who loved him. We will never forget the unimaginable loss they continue to carry. But we also remember Charlie for how he lived. Charlie’s faith was at the center of who he was. His faith in Christ was his armor, which no assassin could overcome. He believed in life everlasting, and that unshakable faith gave him a courage impossible to miss. He wanted others to know the hope and truth he had in Jesus. Charlie died a martyr for Christ. Charlie believed America was worth fighting for, that young people could change the course of a nation, and that speech would only remain free if exercised. He was fearless in the pursuit of truth, no matter the cost. Turning Point shares those beliefs and will never abandon them. Charlie never gave up, and neither will we. Today, we remember an incredible patriot, a husband, a father, and a man whose faith gave him the courage to spend his life serving a purpose bigger than himself. We miss him. We grieve him. And we will never forget him. One year later, Turning Point remains committed to carrying forward the work Charlie began. For Charlie. Always. | tK1JZ5B.com

items.author: Philana Nowak
items.bodyText: Ashley Goodwin it’s obvious you don’t work in a school. I have seen these kids bypass the school security all the time. NOTHING HAPPENS. It’s like 3 clicks and they get onto sites that are forbidden. I can’t access any social media (I sub), connected to guest WiFi, but kids can get just about anywhere. If a kid doesn’t have access at home, the school can make special arrangements if assignments requirement it. I heard a stat that 99% of the people have smartphones, which means they have WiFi access in some way. But I advocate getting rid of 1:1 tech for all kids-bring back pen and paper. Most of my kids’ teachers did and have found retention of material has improved tremendously. They only use Chromebooks for tests, which does not require a 1:1 scenario.

items.author: MissMegan L Donelli
items.bodyText: This sounds absolutely accurate. Unions don't have as much power as you think they do----- and if a school wants a teacher out --- even a tenured one because they don't like them , whatever--- they will make up a case, say they can't comment on personnel cases, --- some districts won't even disclose to the accused employee "what" they "did", they tell them they'll find out after their investigation is completed. They use fear tactics. They forbid the accused employee from talking to anyone in the district. They deactivate their email accounts immediately, so the employee can't access any evidence that would be in their favor. Think it doesn't happen? Think again! I've been teaching almost 30 years and I've SEEN these set ups happen to innocent and amazing teachers who "someone" doesn't like for whatever reason. Could be a principal. Could be a co-worker who has connections to a board member or is married to an Admin or someone who works at the District Office, could be an entitled parent who hates the teacher bc their child didn't get an "A", and the parent has connections, is loud, runs their mouth on Social Media, or calls local newspapers or TV channels---threatens lawsuits. It HAPPENS. School Districts do NOT care about their teachers as human beings. The first priority is ALWAYS THE DISTRICT and its money and its reputation. No bad media attention! It's not the kids either--- lol. They care about kids who can get them GOOD PUBLICITY. That's why if the parent of a star athlete is unhappy--- they will do ANYTHING to keep that parent happy. I asked my Chat GPT yesterday if its only function was to have a career and be either a Nurse, a Teacher, a Therapist, or a Fire Fighter, and to explain its choice, rank the choices, and to discuss all pros and cons. It chose teaching dead last and it had over 150 cons. It said that in 2026, the US education system was outdated and would never meet the needs of ALL school aged children in the country. It said it could only consider education as a career if there were a major overhaul of the entire Public K-12 school system, including issues like truly raising the pay for teachers based on the amount of responsibilities they have at school every DAY, paying them for all of the hours teachers work every day-- even those worked at home-- grading, lesson planning, creating activities & materials etc, having the autonomy to teach in their own way, style, and choices of materials and curriculum. (State grade level standards must be covered-- as that is mandated by the state). Lower class sizes. More Recess. Enough special education staff.Trauma-Informed staff. Making a distinction between students who have learning disabilities and need the support of special education, and students who have experienced so much childhood trauma that their behavior is disrupting their education and the education of other students in their classrooms. There should be IEP's, 504 Plans, and a new program for Traumatized students who need Behavioral support. Determinations can be made whether these students are best served in Gen Ed classrooms, or if they need to be in smaller classrooms with specialized teaching staff along with Supportive teaching aides or paraprofessionals. And for God Sake Supportive Admin.who do their own jobs instead of micromanaging teachers.

items.author: Randy Mousley
items.bodyText: Most of this is a pretty comprehensive copy/paste.One question for you. Where in her description of the incident does she say her WNEA rep advised to sign. What I read was there was no WNEA representation.As for the alleged union breach of duty. It’s called fair representation. It really only applies in breach of contract issues. It means that the Bargaining Unit agent, in this case the WNEA, has the obligation to defend the contract equally for both dues paying members and non-paying free riders. A possibly unlawful termination wouldn’t necessarily be a breach of contract unless the negotiated agreement contains language outlining a very specific due process procedure above what might be delineate in Missouri state statute. She never says if she was a WNEA member, whether she apprised them of her situation, or if they denied representation or not. Yes, membership status does matter, as does the affirmative action of apprising the bargaining agent.I know a little about these things, spent six years-full time release as the local president in the largest school district in the Midwest and VP of the state organization as well as working at the national level. I don’t know everything about teacher representation, but I know more than most. It’s never as simple as those wronged want it to be.That being said, I concur that she should seek independent counsel.

items.author: Karin Fitzgerald Robinette
items.bodyText: Since you called me out in this post… please note at the time of the review there were two copies available in district libraries at the high school level. The district had to purchase enough copies for all of the reviewers to have it (I.e. wasted money). Here are my takeaways after reading every word of the entire book; not just select lines or single words that fit the challenge argument posed to us. Isolated jokes or foul language do not define the book's true purpose to help young readers understand how adolescents cope with a dying peer. Like it or not, this is a reality for many teens. The swearing and awkward humor reflect how high schoolers genuinely talk. Spend time at any high school sporting event to witness how they communicate with each other. Stripping away this realism makes characters less relatable to students, especially those who may not be avid readers. It’s important to note the main characters are virgins and there are no actual sex scenes in the text. Libraries exist to provide a broad range of perspectives. Restricting books based on complaints about language prevents students from choosing materials that resonate with their personal experiences. As you stated in your post, parents have the ability to restrict content for their own children. I’m grateful the district provides this avenue for parents who want to shield their children from the real world.

items.author: Ashley Tatro Hagerty
items.bodyText: I would like to encourage you to obtain your substitute teacher certification and witness the amount of work they handle. Each middle school has roughly 3 principals, and we have Hollenbeck and Barnwell feeding in to FHN. There are 1,716 students enrolled at FHN. If you divide that by the number of principals (7), that averages 245 students per principal. I have a hunch the activities director doesn’t have much student contact, so let’s divide it by 6 and get 286 students per principal. Now imagine all of these events take place: 10% have IEP meetings that need attended, lunches need monitored, discipline needs addressed, teachers need observed, supervision needs to occur throughout the school, business meetings need to be attended, etc. This is only scratching the surface of their duties. I would personally rather have a school “overstaffed” (which it isn’t) than understaffed.

items.bodyText: Could not agree with you more.I was a member of NEA for three years and was a building rep the third year. It was 1979 in Hazelwood. We went on strike for two years which of course, as you know is completely illegal. items.author: Alyssa Gill
items.bodyText: This is reading as tone deaf. Whether you want to admit it or not, many middle schoolers and high schoolers do struggle with suicidal ideation, substance abuse and all kinds of sexual byproducts. YA books featuring topics on mental health struggles and substance abuse is realistic. Pretending like it doesn’t happen doesn’t make it go away. For kids struggling, being able to connect with a character who shares their struggles can be the thing that keeps them going. You’ve no idea how powerful books are for teenagers. When it feels like no one else gets it, a character in a book understands. It can be something to lessen the isolation feeling. And you’d be lying to yourselves pretending that teens don’t have sex. They do. They will and they are. The least we can do is INFORM them because they’re going to do it anyway. Approaching the issue by educating them on what safe and consensual sex looks like is better than pretending they don’t have sex at all. I don’t enjoy the thought of teens having sex like the next person, but I at LEAST want them to do so safely and consensually when they do.

The legit concerns are there but this is how we prep our kids for the future. Whether we agree with it or not on that’s how our future should be-it is what it is. I think they also have safety measures and parental controls on it in a sense, where they can’t access certain websites and can’t just put anything on the tablets, I think the district already has blocked sites and apps. So the kids can’t just hop on there and play Roblox or anything crazy like that.

items.author: Maya K Crawford
items.bodyText: Randy Mousley "Her NEA attorney told her to sign." That's the only spot where representation actually gets mentioned in connection with the signing itself.But you're onto something — it doesn't really line up with the rest of what she's saying. There are two separate claims getting mashed together here:"Zero representation in the meetings that decided her career" — that's about the Board/admin meetings where they hashed out the termination."Her NEA attorney told her to sign" — that's about the separation agreement, after the fact.So technically, the post isn't saying NEA was nowhere to be found. It's saying she had no rep in the room while the decision was being made, but an NEA attorney did weigh in later on whether to sign the waiver. Those two things can both be true at once — they're not really a contradiction. But smashing them together under "zero union defense" makes it sound way more absolute than what she's actually describing.And your read on fair representation holds up. DFR is about the union defending the contract for the whole bargaining unit — dues-payers and free riders alike. Getting isolated over health comments and pushed into a bad separation deal isn't automatically a breach of that duty unless the CBA has due-process language that goes beyond what Missouri statute already gives tenured teachers. Plus she never says whether she was even a member, or if/when she told WNEA what was happening — and both of those would matter a lot if she tried to bring a DFR claim.

items.author: Amalyn Martin
items.bodyText: I cannot wrap my head around this man simply being out in the community after reading that probable cause statement. According to the filing, he allegedly discussed the bodies of middle school girls, talked about sexual contact with his own daughter, and then characterized these conversations as “fantasy.” What the fuck does that even mean when you are a middle school principal with daily access to children? Even if he is presumed innocent until proven guilty, public safety still matters. When the allegations themselves involve sexual interest in children — especially children the same age as the students entrusted to you — I do not understand why the default is simply “bond out and go home.” If a court has credible evidence that someone may be capable of harming children, that person should not have ordinary access to children while the case is pending. And if they are ultimately convicted, serving a sentence should not automatically mean they are suddenly safe to be around kids again. Treatment, risk assessment, supervision and proof of rehabilitation should matter. And what school district would ever feel comfortable putting someone back around children after even discussing this rancid shit as a “fantasy”? Children should not be the experiment used to determine whether an adult is safe. Protect them first.

items.author: Maya K Crawford
items.bodyText: In Missouri, a tenured teacher who was pushed out under claimed duress, health discrimination, or uncommunicated allegations faces complex legal terrain—especially after signing a separation agreement waiving tenure rights.​Under Missouri state and federal law, a signed separation agreement and waiver can potentially be challenged, set aside, or bypassed depending on the specific legal theories pursued.​1. Legal Pathways to Challenge or Setting Aside the Separation Agreement​Ordinarily, a signed release or resignation agreement bars future lawsuits. However, several legal doctrines under Missouri law can invalidate or limit the enforceability of such agreements:​Duress, Coercion, and Undue Influence:Under Missouri contract law, an agreement executed under severe economic, emotional, or physical duress can be voided. Courts examine whether the individual was deprived of free will, especially if the district took advantage of severe medical vulnerability or recent cancer treatments to force a rapid signature under threat of immediate destruction of her career or reputation.​Lack of Knowing and Voluntary Waiver (ADEA / OWBPA Standards if Applicable):If age discrimination or statutory disability waivers are involved, strict requirements govern whether a release was "knowing and voluntary." If the district concealed material facts—such as serious accusations ("kidnapping") that formed the underlying basis for their actions—the waiver may be vulnerable to a claim of fraudulent inducement or misrepresentation.​Fraudulent Inducement / Concealment:If school officials concealed the true reasons for their actions, made false representations regarding health costs/status, or misrepresented the nature of the allegations to extract a quick signature, the release can be invalidated on grounds of fraud.​2. Substantive Legal Claims Available Under Missouri & Federal Law​If the separation agreement is invalidated—or for claims that fall outside the scope of the waiver—she can explore several causes of action:​A. Disability / Health Discrimination & Retaliation​Missouri Human Rights Act (MHRA - RSMo § 213.055):It is illegal for an employer to discriminate against an employee based on a history of disability/cancer or perceived disability ("regarded as" having a disability).​If the Superintendent made statements to the Board speculating or claiming her cancer had returned, or if her past high-cost medical treatments were a motivating factor in removing her to lower self-insured district costs, this supports a strong claim for disability discrimination and interference under the MHRA.​Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) / Rehabilitation Act:Federal parallel claims prohibiting adverse employment actions based on actual disability, record of disability, or perceived disability.​B. Due Process & Missouri Teacher Tenure Act Violations​Missouri Teacher Tenure Act (RSMo §§ 168.102 – 168.130):Tenured teachers in Missouri possess a constitutionally protected property interest in their employment. Under Missouri law, a district cannot terminate a tenured teacher without:​Detailed written charges;​A minimum 30-day notice period;​A formal public or private hearing before the Board of Education with the right to counsel, cross-examination, and sub-poena power.​Constitutional Due Process (42 U.S.C. § 1983):If district officials conspired to bypass statutory tenure protections by creating a coercive environment, isolating her, imposing gag orders, and withholding charges until after securing a coerced resignation, she may bring a Section 1983 claim for deprivation of procedural due process.​C. Defamation and Tortious Interference​Defamation / Slander Per Se:False statements alleging serious criminal conduct (such as "kidnapping") or unverified medical status communicated to third parties (like the School Board) without privilege can constitute actionable defamation under Missouri law.​Violation of Public Records / Sunshine Law Issues:Improper executive session statements or board communications regarding medical history may violate state privacy standards or the Missouri Sunshine Law governing closed meetings.​3. Immediate Actionable Steps She Can Take​Retain Independent Employment Counsel immediately:Since the union (NEA) attorney advised signing, she needs a private plaintiff-side employment and civil rights attorney specializing in Missouri public school law, MHRA litigation, and setting aside release agreements.​File Charges with Administrative Agencies (Time-Sensitive):​MCHR / EEOC: Before filing an MHRA or ADA lawsuit, an administrative charge of discrimination must be filed with the Missouri Commission on Human Rights (MCHR) or the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC).​Crucial Stricter Timelines: Under Missouri law, MHRA charges must generally be filed within 180 days of the discriminatory act. EEOC deadlines are up to 300 days.​Preserve All Evidence & Records:​Gather all emails, text messages, Google Docs logs, medical records confirming remission, and notes from meetings.​Request her complete personnel file under Missouri law.​Submit formal Missouri Sunshine Law (RSMo Chapter 610) public records requests for all emails between district administrators, board members, and legal counsel regarding her employment, health/insurance costs, and the incident in question.​Report Union Breach of Duty (If Applicable):If union representatives failed to provide adequate representation or colluded in pressuring her into signing an invalid waiver under duress, she can consult her attorney regarding potential breach of duty claims or reporting options.​Deepening This Topic

items.author: Amy RB
items.bodyText: Nic Peña sex (i.e., DNA) is different from gender/identity (brain development/structure). Our brains develop at different times in utero than genitalia and are sensitive to maternal hormone fluctuations. Trans people tend to have brains that are more similar to the other sex than the sex they were identified as at birth. And being trans is legit and not a mental illness, according to the experts on mental illness and the brain in multiple branches of scientific disciplines.

items.author: Shannon Senzig
items.bodyText: Julie Layton They don't have to be "big books like back in the day," though. That's a false dichotomy. Those books were designed with longevity in mind. They were expected to last for 15 years, so they were hardbound and huge. As a result, lots of schools had to make due with damaged, old, and out of date books that the students had to copy from. What we need are smaller, paperback, single use work books for each student. These have always been around, but the hardbound mega-books were thought to be cheaper so most school districts went that route, with maybe the exception being spelling. Remembering hand copying all those math problems and grammar lessons into a notebook? And pages and pages of wasted space full of illustrations and fluff to justify making the book as expensive as possible? That was completely unnecessary and not what was best for kids. Meanwhile, subjects that do require a text such as science and social studies can be done online in the classroom and study guides can be sent home instead.

items.author: R G Julie Burr
items.bodyText: Guessing you’ve not been a para for some of our most challenging students. I did it for 11 years straight with an advanced degree and licensed as a clinical social worker. I’d probably have made more at McDonald’s and was assaulted multiple times. I sensed God wanted me to continue serving these precious souls but MANY para’s left for other districts that pay almost DOUBLE! By law, FHSD CANNOT just say, “you’re a messed up kid, so stay home.” Puhleeeze don’t even begin to proselytize that which you may have zilch personal info to back up your claims. My sister has spent her little money as a teacher to literally take bags of groceries to a student’s house so that they could eat better to be more equipped to learn. Not every family is equally resourced! How many hours a week do you volunteer to read to these students? Do you volunteer in the cafeteria? How much period blood have you wiped from a non verbal student? How much poop have you cleaned from shoe treads after prepping a student for PE? Ivory tower platitudes have no place in this conversation.

items.bodyText: ￼ And pretty much the person who was fired as an idiot. I hate to say it again after teaching for 33 years never being a member of NEA because they won’t protect you they won’t do anything..If you get your own lawyer, you’ll do fine.I never had to because I never kidnapped an 18 year-old so no matter what you think Brian you definitely don’t have all the facts no one ever does.A terrible thing to happen for all the people involved, including the 18-year-old.Please remember you do not and I mean do not have all the facts. items.author: School Watchlist
items.bodyText: Ashley Goodwin Equal access matters, but a school-issued Chromebook isn’t the only (or safest) way to provide it. Proving to only families in need would be cost efficient and logical. Monitoring school Wi-Fi doesn’t cover off-network use, personal accounts, or apps students add themselves. A family smartphone is parent-controlled; a district device is not.Most classes no longer issue a full set of physical textbooks, so the backpack-weight comparison doesn’t hold. The real differences are distraction, screen time, content students can reach, and how much visibility parents actually have.

items.author: Chris Martens
items.bodyText: School Watchlist Missouri actually does have a law intended to prevent this. In 2011, Missouri passed the Amy Hestir Student Protection Act, which includes 162.068 RSMo. Under that law, a district hiring a teacher who previously worked in a Missouri public school must check with DESE and request information from the most recent district. The law also addresses situations where an employee resigns instead of being fired because of sexual-misconduct allegations and can hold a former district liable if it conceals qualifying information and the employee later harms a student elsewhere.
